concept.definition: Batch Normalization is a technique that normalizes the activations of a layer across a mini-batch to have zero mean and unit variance, followed by a learned affine transformation, to stabilize and accelerate training.
concept.simpleExplanation: It adjusts the outputs of a layer so they have a consistent scale and center, which prevents values from becoming too large or too small. This makes the network more stable and allows it to learn faster with higher learning rates.
concept.analogy: Imagine a factory assembly line where each workstation receives parts that vary wildly in size. Batch Normalization is like adding a standardizer that resizes each part to a uniform size before passing it on, making the job of each workstation easier and more predictable.
concept.whyUsedHere: The paper uses BN after every convolution and before activation to enable training of very deep networks (e.g., 152 layers) by mitigating the vanishing/exploding gradient problem and allowing higher learning rates without divergence.
